### Added
- **The LLM listener routes by model: every `llmRouting.models` entry is an `AgentgatewayModel` attached directly to the data plane's LLM listener, and served models join it through the LLMEndpoint document** (giantswarm/agent-platform#603). The request's `model` picks the model; the default list is `anthropic` (provider Anthropic, `baseURL: https://api.anthropic.com/v1` — agentgateway 2.1 builds the upstream path from the baseURL's path, and a managed provider without one sends Anthropic `/messages` —, `match: claude-*`), credential-free as the `AgentgatewayBackend` it replaces. The models attach to the Gateway's `llm` listener by `sectionName`, with no `HTTPRoute` and no path prefix in front: agentgateway 2.1.2 strips the matched `PathPrefix` of a rule whose backend is the model router, so a route at `/v1` handed it `/messages`, which it proxied as Passthrough with no `agentgateway_gen_ai_*` token or cost metric, and the Gateway-scoped route-type map overrode its classification for every other path; listener-attached models match the serving endpoints (`/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions`, …), which outrank the MCP catch-all. The in-cluster `HTTPRoute`, the route-type map policy and the `llmRouting.pathPrefixes` and `llmRouting.routes` values are gone; ModelConfig base URLs stay the listener's origin with no path. With LLM routing and a serving model-manager — this release's serving slice, or a GPU node pool's, which comes as a second release of the chart with model-manager off — the chart renders the LLMEndpoint document (ConfigMap `<name>-llm-endpoint`, labelled `agent-platform.giantswarm.io/llm-endpoint: "true"`: `parentRefs` exactly the provider models', `endpoint` the listener's in-cluster URL, `externalEndpoint` with the external endpoint), model-manager's ServiceAccount gets a Role on the release namespace's `agentgatewaymodels` and nothing else, and the data plane's egress reaches the workload pods where model-manager serves (both flavours), so model-manager attaches one `AgentgatewayModel` per served model under its preset's name (giantswarm/model-manager#145); the serving slice's discovery ConfigMap no longer carries `spec.llmEndpoint`, which a node pool's topology never rendered. `llmRouting.external` (off by default) puts the endpoint on `https://llm.<global.domain>` behind the installation's API keys (`apiKeyAuthentication` `Strict` over one Secret or ConfigMap source) on a route at `PathPrefix: /` — a root model route, whose hostname outranks the catch-all: on the data plane's HTTPS listener with the chart's edge, else on a data-plane listener of its own, `llmRouting.external.listener` (`llm-external`, `8082`), to which the public Gateway forwards the hostname and which the data-plane network policies admit from the cluster, since the controller refuses a root model route beside directly attached models; every model attaches to it, the LLMEndpoint document names it, and the data plane's metrics carry each key's `metadata.name` as `api_key`. A key reaches every model until agentgateway enforces `allowedModels` on the Kubernetes contract (the README says so). **Breaking** for an installation that set `llmRouting.backend`, `llmRouting.pathPrefixes` or `llmRouting.routes`: the schema refuses them; see UPGRADE.md. `verify-llm-routing` covers the listener-attached models and their guards (a duplicate name, a wildcard the CRD refuses, an empty list), the absence of the in-cluster route and the routes map, the external route and its listener in both edge shapes, the LLMEndpoint document's content, the Role and the egress with this release's slice and a node pool's, and nothing of it without LLM routing or a serving model-manager.
